page: Microsoft Azure L16s_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the LSv3 family, virtualized via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and cryptography extensions such as AES and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and bundles 4004 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results place the L16s_v3 in the average performance tier for most compute metrics, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks scoring 1899.38 and 15536.57 respectively. Memory performance is a relative strength, with the PassMark memory score categorized in the top 25% at 2765.45, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 834.55 GB/sec. Database operations via PassMark scored 8012.53, and Redis SET operations achieved 15.98 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning, the server processed 135M parameter LLM prompts at 783.53 tokens per second and generated text at 233.65 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L16s_v3 offers a high density of local NVMe storage and memory relative to its 16 vCPUs, making it a viable option for workloads requiring large local scratch space or fast data access without the premium of larger compute instances. However, the CPU performance remains strictly in the average tier, meaning it may not be optimal for compute-bound tasks that do not leverage the local NVMe storage. The server is suited for database hosting, memory-intensive applications, static web serving, and software compilation.
description: Microsoft Azure L16s_v3 is an x86_64 server in the LSv3 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 2.8 GHz. It features 128.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 4004 GB local NVMe SSD. The server delivers average CPU performance, as shown by a PassMark CPU score of 21313.63 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 15536.57. However, its memory subsystem is a relative highlight, achieving a PassMark memory score in the top 25% tier. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial local NVMe storage, this instance provides a balanced profile for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads. It is suited for database operations, Redis deployments, and software compilation, though it lacks GPU acceleration for heavy AI workloads.
